current_episode.title: From Leadership to Legacy: Cyndi Garza on Pivoting, Connection, and Building a Life You Love

guest.entreprise_secondaire: CU Boutique (luxury boutique coffee wine bar)
guest.bio_context: Cyndi Garza started her career as a mortgage loan officer and quickly realized the need for strong leadership. She returned to school to complete her degree, studying management and leadership, and dedicated her career in mortgage banking to becoming a leader others could count on. Along the way, she purchased Mortgage Girlfriends and launched her coaching company Optimize Success approximately 12 years ago. After losing three family members in a short period of time, she decided to retire from the mortgage industry and pivot to starting an online boutique, which eventually evolved into her current luxury boutique coffee wine bar called CU Boutique in Sarasota, Florida.

pending_qa.q: What are the most important pieces of advice for women entrepreneurs or aspiring leaders starting a new venture?
pending_qa.r: The first piece of advice is to seek good coaching or consulting, as it improves not just business but all areas of life. Second, think back to what you enjoyed as a young person—what made you lose track of time—and bring those activities back into your life in small steps. For example, Cyndi loved sitting around a table with family drinking coffee and chatting, so she started going to coffee shops every Wednesday to work, which eventually led to owning a coffee wine bar. Third, do not try to have it all figured out; take small steps in the right direction with accountability support.

pending_qa.q: How can aspiring entrepreneurs reduce the risk of mistakes when launching a new business in an unfamiliar industry?
pending_qa.r: Reach out to people who have already been successful in that field and pick their brain. For her boutique coffee wine bar venture, Cyndi met a woman who had run a successful boutique for 40 years, visited her, spent time learning from her, and called her regularly for advice. That woman later asked Cyndi how she built such a strong team and was able to take a vacation just two weeks after opening—demonstrating the value of mentorship. Building genuine connections with successful people in your target industry and offering to help them in return creates a reciprocal relationship that benefits everyone.

pending_qa.q: What are the ideal client profiles for executive and leadership coaching engagements?
pending_qa.r: One ideal client is the middle manager struggling with relationships both above and below—someone who may be handed goals without input and needs help reframing those goals to engage their team. Another ideal client is the regional senior leader with large teams reporting to them, who needs coaching to build strong leaders around them and orchestrate complex organizational dynamics. A recent example involved coaching a woman to identify and develop her own replacement as she advanced, which initially felt threatening but became empowering once she realized this succession planning elevated her career trajectory.
